title: Why did George Raft fade into Obscurity?

commenti.body:
I think you answered your own question -- he repeatedly turned down what were, in hindsight, iconic roles. Had he taken one of them, he would have had a film that new generations of moviegoers would discover.

And it's only natural that some actors (and actresses, and directors, and writers) will fade into obscurity. So many movies have been made since Raft's prime and, simply put, no one has the time or mental bandwidth to explore all of cinema. Consider Raft's *Scarface* costar Paul Muni. Best Actor winner (with four more nominees), star of a Best Picture winner, one of the most popular and critically acclaimed actors of the 1930s. When's the last time you heard/read anyone discuss him and his films?

I think with Paul Muni- it is with respect for those who have heard of him thanks to his stage roles and many people talking about his dedication to his roles and to his credit has Scarface and Emila Zola, and also people will think of his interesting role in The Good Earth

With George Raft- I think people will think, "Idiot Actor who should of done Maltese Falcon or Double Indemnity".
Re: Paul Muni the narrative you get from, say, David Thomson is that his acting is over-the-top and dated.

But he has heard of Paul Muni.

 to be frank, I have heard of these accusations of Paul Muni being an over-actor, but I also heard from interviews from his peers that he was dedicated to his craft and they respected what he has done

Muni came out of a pre-Stanislavsky/Actor’s Studio era of heightened dramatic technique. He grew up on the Yiddish theatre stage and had a sort of a Lon Chaney Master-of-Disguise reputation. He has his moments of brilliance, but there’s a lot of cringe  (from today’s standpoint) in between. The final scene of I Am a Fugitive From a Chain Gang holds up like crazy.

He really messed up not doing High Sierra. Bogey basically had to BEG for the part and afterwards became a star (people always say Casablanca made him a household name but Sierra showed Bogey could play a criminal with a heart) it’s just a boneheaded move on Raft to not take the part because of the character dying at the end which if you’ve seen the movie you’d know how iconic that ending scene was.

He turned down the lead in The Maltese Falcon    .But it is just as well .Bogie made it a classic. The story goes that he turned down so many  roles the studio just got sick of him    Oddly enough he made a movie with Humphrey Bogart called They Drive By Night.

Muni is actually looked at as exactly the kind of actor that the system/method is supposed to train you to become. I’m pretty sure Stanislavski loved his acting and that he even met the Moscow Art Theatre actors when they were touring New York. Brando was also blown away by him when they acted together in a play.
Funny because a lot of actors looked at Muni as being modern in his acting before modern acting technique became widespread.

As others pointed out you kinda answered. I'll add that as a result of his many refusals, his filmography is solid but lacks movies that modern audience still watches unless you're a movie buff that likes old Hollywood. 

Probably his most famous role nowadays is the gangster in Some Like It Hot, but I don't think that based on that many will think Raft was a major star in the 1930s.

>  Oddly enough he made a movie with Humphrey Bogart called They Drive By Night.

Also *Invisible Stripes* before that.
